cases.element: content.body.scope.noteUk: "з днями тижня прийменник не вживається (не «en lunes»)"
cases.defect: This categorically prohibits prepositions with weekdays. Standard expressions such as "de lunes a viernes", "hasta el lunes" and "caer en lunes" contain prepositions. The basic el/los construction is correct, but the prohibition is too broad.
cases.correction: Limit the statement to simple weekday expressions answering when an event happens: "el lunes" and "los lunes", without en. Acknowledge that other constructions use prepositions.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 29, temporal uses of prepositions (from memory).

cases.reviewerAnswer: Examples: "el cinco de mayo", "el uno de mayo" or "el primero de mayo"; 5/3 denotes 5 March in the stated format.
The twelve month names are correct; "en mayo" and "en verano" express the stated time frames.
Identify the weekday, date or appointment time; assess dictation separately from listening comprehension.
"Cuándo" asks when; "¿A qué hora…?" specifically asks the time.
The dentist example specifies Tuesday, 3 March, at 17:00.
"cita": feminine noun meaning an appointment or arranged meeting; plural "citas".
"cumpleaños": masculine noun meaning "день народження"; unchanged in the plural.
"jueves": masculine noun meaning "четвер"; unchanged in the plural.
"lunes": masculine noun meaning "понеділок"; unchanged in the plural.
"martes": masculine noun meaning "вівторок"; unchanged in the plural.
"miércoles": masculine noun meaning "середа"; unchanged in the plural.
"reunión": feminine noun meaning a meeting or gathering; plural "reuniones".
"septiembre": masculine noun meaning "вересень"; "setiembre" is also a standard spelling.
"viernes": masculine noun meaning "п’ятниця"; unchanged in the plural.
The three instructional stages cover weekdays, months and dates, then appointment questions and times.
"Hoy no es lunes, hoy es martes."

cases.element: task.options[id=b]: "Піти до лікаря в понеділок о п’ятій.", marked incorrect
cases.defect: The distractor depends on an unstated distinction. "Лікар" can denote a medical practitioner generally, including a dentist, or be understood more narrowly as a physician contrasted with a dentist. Under the general reading, both a and b describe the required visit.
cases.correction: Make the distractor unambiguously incompatible with the note, for example by changing its time: "Піти до стоматолога в понеділок о десятій."
